title: Hawaiian Protein Pizza (Justin cut)
imageCredit: Reference stock photo by Shoeib Abolhassani on Unsplash (Unsplash License)
creator: Justin adaptation (Hawaiian-style, no pepperoni)
summary: Classic Hawaiian vibes — Canadian bacon or lean ham / grilled chicken, pineapple, mild veggies — on the high-protein low-carb dough. No pepperoni. Sweet-savory and mild.
whyItFits: High protein from dough + lean meat + part-skim mozzarella
Pineapple for Hawaiian style; optional monk-fruit glaze keeps sugar in check

items: 2–3 tbsp light pizza sauce or crushed tomato (no-added-sugar if possible)
2–3 oz Canadian bacon or lean ham, chopped or
3–4 oz grilled / leftover chicken breast, cubed
1/4–1/3 cup pineapple tidbits, well drained (pat dry)
Optional monk-fruit glaze: toss drained pineapple with a tiny pinch monk fruit + drop of 0-sugar simple syrup, or brush a light glaze after bake
Optional: pinch dried oregano or Italian seasoning (mild)

steps: Make and par-bake the LC cottage-cheese dough per the dough recipe (425°F until set).
Spread a thin layer of light pizza sauce or tomato on the hot crust.
Add half the mozzarella, then Canadian bacon/ham or chicken, pineapple, bell pepper, and red onion.
Bake 8–12 minutes at 425°F until cheese bubbles and edges brown. Optional brief broil.
Optional: light monk-fruit / 0-sugar syrup glaze on pineapple bits. Rest 2 minutes, slice.
substitutions: No pepperoni: Canadian bacon, lean ham, or grilled chicken only.
Sweeteners: monk fruit or 0-sugar simple syrup (sucralose) for a light pineapple glaze — skip if pineapple is sweet enough.
Lower cal: lighter sauce layer, part-skim mozzarella, lean chicken over ham.
Extra protein: more chicken + the whey option in the dough.
Veggies: add spinach under the cheese if you want more greens without changing the Hawaiian profile much.
notes: Drain pineapple well — excess juice softens the LC crust.
Keep seasoning mild; Hawaiian is sweet-savory, not spicy.
Full dough batch → two personal Hawaiian pizzas, or one larger thin pie.
Dough source reel is often wheat-based viral cottage cheese dough; Justin cut uses almond flour — see dough recipe notes.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate for 1 personal pizza with half LC dough, lean ham/chicken, part-skim mozzarella, drained pineapple. Not lab-tested.

title: High-Protein Low-Carb Pizza Dough (Justin cut)
imageCredit: Reference stock photo by Aldward Castillo on Unsplash (Unsplash License)
creator: unknown (viral cottage cheese dough reel)
summary: Viral cottage-cheese pizza doughs often blend cottage cheese with wheat flour — tasty, but not low-carb. This Justin cut keeps the blended cottage-cheese base and swaps in fine almond flour (plus egg + baking powder) for a high-protein, low-carb thin crust that still browns and holds toppings.
whyItFits: High protein from cottage cheese (+ optional mozzarella / whey)
Low-carb: almond flour instead of wheat
Mild — no spice in the dough
Makes ~2 personal-pizza servings (or one medium thin crust)
Base for Hawaiian and BBQ-honey chicken pizzas

items: 1 cup (about 220 g) low-fat cottage cheese, blended smooth
1 cup (about 96–112 g) fine almond flour (blanched preferred)
Optional for structure / chew: 1/4–1/2 cup (28–56 g) shredded part-skim mozzarella, mixed into the dough

steps: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a sheet pan or pizza stone with parchment; lightly spray.
Blend cottage cheese until completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor). No lumps.
In a bowl, mix blended cottage cheese, egg, almond flour, baking powder, salt, and optional mozzarella until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Rest 2–3 minutes so almond flour hydrates.
Divide in half for two personal pizzas (or keep whole for one larger thin crust). With wet or lightly oiled hands, press into thin rounds (~1/4 inch / 6 mm) on the parchment — thinner crisps better.
Par-bake 8–12 minutes until the surface looks set and edges start to lightly brown. (This is the sturdy-crust step — don’t skip.)
Add sauce + toppings, then bake another 8–12 minutes until cheese melts and crust edges are golden. For extra crisp, broil 1–2 minutes at the end (watch closely).
substitutions: Coconut flour caution: do not 1:1 swap. Coconut flour is much more absorbent; if using, start with ~1/4–1/3 cup and add egg or a splash of water until dough presses thinly — texture will be different.
Whey protein optional boost: 1–2 tbsp unflavored whey mixed into the dough for extra protein; may dry the dough slightly — add a spoon of cottage cheese or water if needed.
Dairy-free: this recipe leans on cottage cheese; not a natural fit — use a preferred LC crust instead.
Flour: stick to fine almond flour for the LC cut; wheat versions of the viral dough are higher carb.
Sweeteners: not needed in the dough. Use stevia / monk fruit / 0-sugar syrup on sweet toppings (BBQ-honey, pineapple glaze) separately.
notes: Viral Facebook reel source often shows wheat-flour cottage cheese dough — not LC. This file is the almond-flour Justin adaptation.
Drain very wet cottage cheese briefly if it looks watery after blending.
If dough tears when pressing, add 1–2 tbsp more almond flour.
Par-bake is key for a thin sturdy crust that won’t go soggy under sauce.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate per personal crust (1/2 dough batch), dough only; optional mozzarella not included. Almond flour + low-fat cottage cheese. Not lab-tested.
